docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This library provides a BSD-style socket API for Orix OS, enabling network communication on Oric computers equipped with a CH395 Ethernet controller. It implements standard socket operations for creating, connecting, sending, and receiving data over TCP and UDP protocols.

Key Features: - TCP (SOCK_STREAM) and UDP (SOCK_DGRAM) socket support - IPv4 protocol (AF_INET) - Standard BSD socket API compatibility - Automatic source port allocation to prevent connection conflicts - Support for up to 8 simultaneous sockets (CH395 hardware limitation)

docs.title: Hardware Requirements
docs.text:
• Oric computer (Atmos, Stratos, Telestrat, or compatible)
  • Orix OS installed
  • CH395 Ethernet controller properly configured
  • Network infrastructure (router, DHCP server recommended)

docs.title: socket()
docs.text:
Create a new socket endpoint for communication.

Prototype: 

unsigned char socket(unsigned char domain, unsigned char type, unsigned char protocol);

Parameters: - domain: Address family (AF_INET for IPv4) - type: Socket type (SOCK_STREAM for TCP, SOCK_DGRAM for UDP) - protocol: Protocol (0 for default, or IPPROTO_TCP/IPPROTO_UDP)

Returns: - Socket descriptor (0-7) on success - INVALID_SOCKET (255) on error

Example: 

unsigned char sock = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
if (sock == INVALID_SOCKET) {
    // Error handling
}

Notes: - Protocol parameter is currently not fully handled - Maximum of 8 sockets can be created (CH395 limitation)

docs.title: bind()
docs.text:
Bind a socket to a local address and port.

Prototype: 

unsigned char bind(unsigned char socket, const struct sockaddr_in* addr, unsigned int addrlen);

Parameters: - socket: Socket descriptor - addr: Pointer to sockaddr_in structure with local address and port - addrlen: Length of the address structure

Returns: - 0 on success - Error code on failure

Status: Work in Progress (WIP) - Not fully functional

Example: 

struct sockaddr_in local_addr;
local_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
local_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
local_addr.sin_port = htons(8080);

if (bind(sock, &local_addr, sizeof(local_addr)) != 0) {
    // Error handling
}

docs.title: connect()
docs.text:
Establish a connection to a remote socket.

Prototype: 

unsigned char connect(unsigned char sockfd, const struct sockaddr *addr, unsigned int addrlen);

Parameters: - sockfd: Socket descriptor - addr: Pointer to sockaddr structure with remote address - addrlen: Length of the address structure

Returns: - 0 on success - Error code on failure

Example: 

struct sockaddr_in server;
server.sin_family = AF_INET;
server.sin_addr.s_addr = inet_addr("192.168.1.100");
server.sin_port = htons(80);

if (connect(sock, (struct sockaddr*)&server, sizeof(server)) != 0) {
    // Connection failed
}

Important Behavior:

Each call to connect() automatically allocates a source port from the range 170 to 425 (170 + $FF). The source port is incremented after each connection to prevent conflicts. This is necessary because when connecting to the same host repeatedly, the remote computer may still be closing the previous connection from the same source port, which would cause the new connection to be rejected.

docs.title: send()
docs.text:
Send data on a connected socket.

Prototype: 

unsigned int send(unsigned char sockfd, const void *buf, unsigned int len, unsigned char flags);

Parameters: - sockfd: Socket descriptor - buf: Pointer to data buffer - len: Number of bytes to send - flags: Send flags (currently not implemented, use 0)

Returns: - Number of bytes sent on success - SOCKET_ERROR (255) on error

Example: 

char request[] = "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n";
int bytes_sent = send(sock, request, strlen(request), 0);
if (bytes_sent == SOCKET_ERROR) {
    // Error handling
}

Notes: - Flags parameter is not currently handled - Blocking operation - waits for data to be sent

docs.title: recv()
docs.text:
Receive data from a connected socket.

Prototype: 

unsigned int recv(unsigned char s, void *buf, unsigned int len, unsigned char flags);

Parameters: - s: Socket descriptor - buf: Pointer to buffer to store received data - len: Maximum number of bytes to receive - flags: Receive flags (currently not implemented, use 0)

Returns: - Number of bytes received (can be 0 if connection closed) - SOCKET_ERROR (255) on error - ETIMEDOUT if operation timed out

Example: 

char buffer[1024];
int bytes_received = recv(sock, buffer, sizeof(buffer) - 1, 0);
if (bytes_received > 0) {
    buffer[bytes_received] = '\0';
    printf("Received: %s", buffer);
} else if (bytes_received == 0) {
    // Connection closed by peer
} else {
    // Error
}

docs.title: sendto()
docs.text:
Send data to a specific destination on a datagram socket.

Prototype: 

int sendto(unsigned char sockfd, const void *buf, size_t len, unsigned char flags,
           const struct sockaddr *dest_addr, socklen_t addrlen);

Parameters: - sockfd: Socket descriptor - buf: Pointer to data buffer - len: Number of bytes to send - flags: Send flags (not implemented) - dest_addr: Pointer to sockaddr structure with destination address - addrlen: Length of the address structure

Returns: - Number of bytes sent on success - SOCKET_ERROR on error

Example (UDP): 

struct sockaddr_in dest;
dest.sin_family = AF_INET;
dest.sin_addr.s_addr = inet_addr("192.168.1.100");
dest.sin_port = htons(53);  // DNS port

sendto(sock, query, query_len, 0, (struct sockaddr*)&dest, sizeof(dest));

Notes: - Automatically calls CONNECT before SEND for the specified destination - Useful for connectionless sockets (UDP)

docs.title: recvfrom()
docs.text:
Receive data and get the source address.

Prototype: 

int recvfrom(unsigned char sockfd, void *buf, size_t len, unsigned char flags,
             struct sockaddr *src_addr, socklen_t *addrlen);

Parameters: - sockfd: Socket descriptor - buf: Pointer to buffer to store received data - len: Maximum number of bytes to receive - flags: Receive flags (not implemented) - src_addr: Pointer to sockaddr structure to store source address - addrlen: Pointer to length of address structure (input/output)

Returns: - Number of bytes received - SOCKET_ERROR on error

Example: 

struct sockaddr_in sender;
socklen_t sender_len = sizeof(sender);
char buffer[1024];

int bytes = recvfrom(sock, buffer, sizeof(buffer), 0,
                    (struct sockaddr*)&sender, &sender_len);

docs.title: socket_close()
docs.text:
Close a socket and release its resources.

Prototype: 

unsigned int socket_close(unsigned char sockfd);

Parameters: - sockfd: Socket descriptor to close

Returns: - 0 on success - Error code on failure

Example: 

socket_close(sock);
sock = INVALID_SOCKET;

Important: Always close sockets when done to free CH395 resources for new connections.

docs.title: TCP Client Example
docs.text:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>

int main() {
    unsigned char sock;
    struct sockaddr_in server;
    char buffer[1024];
    int bytes_received;

    // Create socket
    sock = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if (sock == INVALID_SOCKET) {
        printf("Socket creation failed\n");
        return 1;
    }

    // Setup server address
    server.sin_family = AF_INET;
    server.sin_addr.s_addr = inet_addr("142.251.156.119");  // google.com
    server.sin_port = htons(80);  // HTTP port

    // Connect to server
    if (connect(sock, (struct sockaddr*)&server, sizeof(server)) != 0) {
        printf("Connection failed\n");
        socket_close(sock);
        return 1;
    }

    // Send HTTP request
    const char *request = "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: google.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n";
    if (send(sock, request, strlen(request), 0) == SOCKET_ERROR) {
        printf("Send failed\n");
        socket_close(sock);
        return 1;
    }

    // Receive response
    while ((bytes_received = recv(sock, buffer, sizeof(buffer) - 1, 0)) > 0) {
        buffer[bytes_received] = '\0';
        printf("%s", buffer);
    }

    // Close socket
    socket_close(sock);
    return 0;
}

docs.title: Source Port Allocation
docs.text:
Important: This library implements automatic source port allocation to prevent connection conflicts:

  • Each call to connect() allocates a source port from the range 170 to 425 (170 + $FF = 170 + 255)
  • The source port is automatically incremented after each connection
  • This prevents issues when reconnecting to the same host

Rationale: When connecting to the same host repeatedly, the remote computer may still be in the process of closing the previous connection from the same source port. The TCP protocol requires a TIME_WAIT state (typically 2*MSL or about 4 minutes) before a port can be reused for the same destination. By incrementing the source port, we avoid this limitation.

Example: 

// First connection uses source port 170
connect(sock1, &server, sizeof(server));

// Second connection uses source port 171
connect(sock2, &server, sizeof(server));

// After 256 connections, wraps back to 170

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Common error codes returned by socket operations:

EPROTOTYPE      = 41  // Protocol wrong type
ESOCKTNOSUPPORT = 44  // Socket type not supported
EPFNOSUPPORT    = 46  // Protocol family not supported
EAFNOSUPPORT    = 47  // Address family not supported
EADDRINUSE      = 48  // Address already in use
ENETDOWN        = 50  // Network is down
ENETUNREACH     = 51  // Network is unreachable
ECONNRESET      = 54  // Connection reset by peer
EISCONN         = 56  // Socket is already connected
ENOTCONN        = 57  // Socket is not connected
ETIMEDOUT       = 60  // Connection timed out
ECONNREFUSED    = 61  // Connection refused
EHOSTUNREACH    = 65  // No route to host

docs.title: CH395-Specific Notes
docs.text:
The CH395 controller has the following characteristics:

  • Maximum Sockets: 8 simultaneous sockets
  • Protocols: TCP, UDP, IP RAW, MAC RAW
  • Buffer Size: 24KB RAM for send/receive buffers
  • Features: DHCP, PPPoE, ARP, ICMP, IGMP
  • Speed: 10/100M Ethernet

Socket States (TCP): - CH395_TCP_CLOSED - CH395_TCP_LISTEN - CH395_TCP_SYN_SENT - CH395_TCP_SYN_REVD - CH395_TCP_ESTABLISHED - CH395_TCP_FIN_WAIT_1 - CH395_TCP_FIN_WAIT_2 - CH395_TCP_CLOSE_WAIT - CH395_TCP_CLOSING - CH395_TCP_LAST_ACK - CH395_TCP_TIME_WAIT

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
1. DNS: No built-in DNS resolution (use IP addresses or external resolver)
  2. bind(): Work in progress - not fully functional
  3. Flags: Most flag parameters in send()/recv() are not implemented
  4. Non-blocking: Currently all operations are blocking
  5. AF_UNIX: Unix domain sockets not fully implemented

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
"Socket error, start network" - Solution: Ensure CH395 is properly initialized and network is connected - Check: CH395_DETECTED should return $AA

Connection refused / Connection timed out - Verify server is running and accessible - Check firewall settings - Verify IP address and port

No route to host - Check network connectivity - Verify default gateway configuration

Too many open sockets - Close unused sockets with socket_close() - Maximum of 8 simultaneous sockets (CH395 limitation)

docs.title: Debugging Tips
docs.text:
1. Check CH395 status registers
  2. Verify network cable connection
  3. Test with known-working network services
  4. Use Wireshark or tcpdump to monitor network traffic

docs.title: gethttp
docs.text:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include "../src/include/sys/socket.h"
#include "arpa/inet.h"
#include "inetextend.h"

#define BUFFER_SIZE 1024

char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

int main() {
    unsigned char sock;
    struct sockaddr_in server;
    int bytes_received;
    const char *request;
    int port;
    unsigned char *byte;

    port = 80;

    printf("Create socket in order to get HTTP response from google.com\n");

    // Création du socket
    sock = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if (sock == -1) {
        printf("socket error\n");
        return 1;
    }

    if (sock == 255) {
        printf("Socket error, start network\n");
        return 1;
    }

    printf("Socket created %d\n", sock);

    // 142.251.156.119 is the IP address for google.com
    if (inet_aton("142.251.156.119", &server.sin_addr.s_addr) == 0) {
        printf("invalid ip\n");
    } else {
        printf("valid ip\n");
    }

    server.sin_family = AF_INET;
    server.sin_port = htons(80);


    // Connexion au serveur
    if (connect(sock, (struct sockaddr *)&server, sizeof(server)) != 0) {
        printf("Connection failed!\n");
        return 1;
    }
    printf("Connected\n");

    request = "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: google.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n";
    if (send(sock, request, strlen(request), 0) == -1) {
        perror("Send failed");
        return 1;
    }

    // Recevoir la réponse HTTP

    while ((bytes_received = recv(sock, buffer, BUFFER_SIZE - 1, 0)) > 0) {
        buffer[bytes_received] = '\0';
        printf("%s", buffer);
    }
    if (bytes_received == -1) {
        perror("Error receiving data");
        return 1;
    }

    // Closing socket
    socket_close(sock);
    return 0;

}

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: SOCKET domain, type, protocol

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Open a socket (protocol is not handled yet) (see kernel routine for more information: https://orix-software.github.io/developer_manual/kernel/primitives/xsocket/)

docs.title: Input
docs.text: param Description domain The communication domain (e.g., AF_INET) (adress ex $abcd) type The type of socket (e.g., SOCK_STREAM) (address ex $abcd) protocol The protocol to be used (e.g., IPPROTO_TCP) (address ex $abcd)

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
• Accumulator : The socket file descriptor (sockfd) or -1 on error

Example

 .include "sys/socket.inc" to get 'INVALID_SOCKET' definition
 .include "sys/socket.mac"
 SOCKET domain, type, protocol
 ; A contains the socket file descriptor (sockfd) or -1 on error
 cmp #INVALID_SOCKET
 beq @error
 ; No error
 sta socket_fd
 rts
 @error:
 ; Error
 rts
domain:
 .byt #AF_INET
type:
 .byt #SOCK_STREAM
protocol:
 .byt $00 ; Not handled yet
socket_fd:
 .byt $00

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: CONNECT socket, ip, dest_port

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Connect a socket to a remote address (see kernel routine for more information: https://orix-software.github.io/developer_manual/kernel/primitives/xconnect/)

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
param Description socket The socket file descriptor ip The IP address to connect to (address ex $abcd) 32 bits big endian dest_port The destination port to connect to (address ex $abcd)

Example

 .include "sys/socket.mac"
 CONNECT socket_fd, ip, dest_port
 rts
ip:
 .word $C0A80001 ; 192.168.0.1
dest_port:
 .word $0050 ; 80
socket_fd:
 .byt $00

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Send data through a socket , returns $FF in A if error, else returns EOK in A (see kernel routine for more information: https://orix-software.github.io/developer_manual/kernel/primitives/xsend/)

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
param Description socket The socket file descriptor buffer The buffer containing the data to send (address ex $abcd) length The length of the data to send (address ex $abcd)

Example

 .include "sys/socket.mac"

 SEND socket_fd, buffer, length
 rts
buffer:
 .dsb 1000 ; Buffer address
length:
 .word 1000 ; Buffer length
socket_fd:
 .byt $00

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: RECV socket, buffer

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Receive data from a socket, uses TR0 (see kernel routine for more information: https://orix-software.github.io/developer_manual/kernel/primitives/xrecv/)

docs.title: Input
docs.text: param Description socket The socket file descriptor buffer The buffer to store the received data (address ex $abcd) length The length of the buffer (address ex $abcd)

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
• Y Register : The number of bytes received (low byte in Y, high byte in X)
  • X Register : The number of bytes received (high byte in Y, high byte in X)
  • Accumulator : The status of the operation (EOK on success, or ETIMEDOUT for Timeout)

Example

 .include "sys/socket.mac"
 RECV mysocket, mybuffer, length
 rts
mysocket:
 .byt $00
buffer:
 .dsb 1000
length:
